Q1/Q7 (labetalol's combined alpha+beta blockade) are collapsed onto one concept. Q5 (q238, least likely clinical use of alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonists) is held: the printed key names Benign prostatic hypertrophy, but this same quiz's own Q3 (tamsulosin for BPH via alpha1A selectivity) and Q11 (prazosin confirmed beneficial in BPH) directly contradict BPH as a 'least likely' use -- a printed-key/pharmacology conflict, not resolved by inference.

questions.title: Labetalol antagonises both alpha and beta adrenoceptors
questions.question: A 34-year-old man is prescribed labetalol for hypertension. The effect on the cardiovascular system is a result of its action as an antagonist at which of the following?

explanations.A: Incorrect as the sole answer. Labetalol does antagonise alpha1-adrenoceptors, but this is only part of its action.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the sole answer. Labetalol does antagonise beta-adrenoceptors, but not exclusively -- it also blocks alpha1 receptors.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Labetalol has no significant action at muscarinic cholinoreceptors; its mechanism is entirely adrenergic.
explanations.D: Correct. Labetalol antagonises both alpha1-adrenoceptors and beta-adrenoceptors together. This dual blockade combines the peripheral vasodilation of alpha1 blockade with the reduced heart rate and cardiac output of beta blockade. It is this combined action, not beta blockade alone, that produces labetalol's overall cardiovascular effect.

questions.learning_objective: State that labetalol's cardiovascular effect results from combined alpha- and beta-adrenoceptor antagonism, not beta blockade alone.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Both alpha and beta-adrenoceptors"

questions.title: Prazosin blocks epinephrine's mydriasis
questions.question: Which of the following actions of epinephrine is blocked by prazosin?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Increased heart rate is a beta1-mediated action of epinephrine, unaffected by the alpha1-selective antagonist prazosin.
explanations.B: Correct. Epinephrine produces mydriasis (pupil dilation) by activating alpha1-adrenoceptors on the iris dilator muscle. Prazosin is a selective alpha1 antagonist, so it blocks this specific alpha1-mediated action. Epinephrine's other, non-alpha1-mediated effects are left unaffected by prazosin.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Increased cardiac stroke volume is a beta1-mediated action, not blocked by the alpha1-selective prazosin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Bronchial dilation is a beta2-mediated action, unrelated to the alpha1 receptors prazosin blocks.

questions.learning_objective: Identify mydriasis as the epinephrine action blocked by the alpha1-selective antagonist prazosin, distinct from epinephrine's beta-mediated actions.

questions.title: Tamsulosin's alpha1A selectivity suits BPH
questions.question: One of the following drugs is the most appropriate for treating patients with BPH (benign prostatic hypertrophy) because of selectivity on 1A:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Phenoxybenzamine is a nonselective, irreversible alpha blocker, not one selective for the alpha1A subtype.
explanations.B: Correct. Tamsulosin is selective for the alpha1A receptor subtype, which predominates in prostatic and bladder-neck smooth muscle. This selectivity relaxes prostatic/bladder-neck smooth muscle to relieve BPH's obstructive symptoms, with comparatively less vascular alpha1 blockade than a nonselective agent. It is this alpha1A selectivity, specifically named in the question, that makes tamsulosin the most appropriate choice here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Prazosin is a general alpha1-selective antagonist, but not specifically alpha1A-subtype-selective the way tamsulosin is.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Terazosin, like prazosin, is a general alpha1 antagonist without tamsulosin's specific alpha1A subtype selectivity.

questions.learning_objective: State that tamsulosin's alpha1A subtype selectivity makes it the most appropriate alpha blocker for BPH among nonselective or general alpha1-selective alternatives.

questions.title: Doxazosin's duration of action is 36 hours
questions.question: The duration of action of doxazosin is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Four hours is far shorter than doxazosin's actual duration of action, closer to a short-acting agent.
explanations.B: Correct. Doxazosin has a long duration of action of approximately 36 hours. This long half-life is what allows once-daily dosing in practice. It is this specific figure, longer than shorter-acting alpha blockers, that the question tests.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Two hours is far shorter than doxazosin's actual, long duration of action.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Twelve hours would support twice-daily, not once-daily, dosing, and understates doxazosin's actual duration.

questions.learning_objective: State that doxazosin's duration of action is approximately 36 hours.

questions.hold: Printed key names Benign prostatic hypertrophy as the least likely clinical use of alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonists (Quiz 30 Q5: 'Which of the following is the least likely clinical use for alpha-adrenoceptor antagonists? ... The correct answer is: Benign prostatic hypertrophy'), but this contradicts standard pharmacology and this same quiz's own teaching: alpha1 blockers are a mainstay of BPH treatment by relaxing prostatic/bladder-neck smooth muscle. Q3 of this same quiz (q236) names tamsulosin's alpha1A selectivity as specifically suited to BPH, and Q11 (q244) states as a FALSE statement that prazosin 'is not beneficial in patients with BPH' -- confirming prazosin IS beneficial in BPH. Held per the printed-key-vs-pharmacology-fact conflict rule (same handling as Q19, Q25, Q47, Q166, Q204, Q224 in this lane's earlier clusters), not resolved by inference.

questions.title: Clonidine's presynaptic alpha2 stimulation inhibits NE release
questions.question: Stimulation of presynaptic alpha2 receptors by clonidine results in:

options.A: Inhibition of NEP release from nerve ending.
options.B: Inhibition of Ach release from cholinergic neurons.
options.C: Inhibition of the uptake of NE.
options.D: Enhancement of release of NEP from nerve endings.

explanations.A: Correct. Presynaptic alpha2-adrenoceptors act as autoreceptors, providing negative feedback on the sympathetic nerve ending's own transmitter release. Clonidine stimulates these presynaptic alpha2 receptors, which inhibits further release of norepinephrine from the nerve ending. This negative-feedback mechanism underlies clonidine's centrally-mediated antihypertensive effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Presynaptic alpha2 receptors on a sympathetic (adrenergic) nerve ending act on that nerve's own norepinephrine release, not on acetylcholine release from a separate cholinergic neuron.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Inhibiting the uptake of norepinephrine describes a different pharmacological action (e.g. of a reuptake inhibitor), not the receptor-mediated feedback effect of alpha2 stimulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This reverses the actual effect -- alpha2 autoreceptor stimulation inhibits, not enhances, further norepinephrine release.

questions.learning_objective: State that clonidine's stimulation of presynaptic alpha2 autoreceptors inhibits further norepinephrine release from the sympathetic nerve ending.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Inhibition of NEP release from nerve ending."

questions.title: Labetalol's alpha1 blockade distinguishes it from propranolol
questions.question: Labetalol is an effective antihypertensive agent that, like propranolol, is capable of blocking beta receptors. An important difference between the two drugs is that labetalol:

options.A: is available only for intravenous use
options.B: is a selective blocker of cardiac B1 receptors.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Labetalol is available in both oral and intravenous formulations, not intravenous-only.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Labetalol is not a selective beta1 blocker -- it is a nonselective beta blocker combined with alpha1 blockade, unlike a cardioselective agent.
explanations.C: Correct. Labetalol's key distinguishing feature from a pure beta-blocker like propranolol is that it also has alpha1-receptor blocking actions. This dual alpha1/beta blockade adds peripheral vasodilation to the reduced heart rate and cardiac output of beta blockade alone. Propranolol has no such alpha1-blocking action, making this the important pharmacological difference between the two drugs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Labetalol does not have intrinsic sympathomimetic activity; that property belongs to a different subset of beta blockers such as acebutolol or pindolol.

questions.learning_objective: Identify alpha1-receptor blocking action as the property that distinguishes labetalol from propranolol, both of which block beta receptors.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: has alpha1 receptor blocking actions"

questions.title: Phentolamine plus nadolol treats pheochromocytoma
questions.question: Pheochromocytoma is better to be treated by:

explanations.A: Incorrect as the best answer among these options. Prazosin plus propranolol does combine alpha1 and beta blockade, but the printed key selects the phentolamine/nadolol pairing as the better combination here.
explanations.B: Correct. Pheochromocytoma's catecholamine excess drives both alpha-mediated vasoconstriction/hypertension and beta-mediated tachycardia. Phentolamine (an alpha antagonist) combined with nadolol (a beta antagonist) supplies both an alpha- and a beta-blocking component together, controlling both arms of the catecholamine excess. This combined alpha-plus-beta approach is the standard management principle for pheochromocytoma.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Phenoxybenzamine and phentolamine are both alpha blockers with no beta-blocking component between them, leaving the tumour's beta-mediated tachycardia unaddressed.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Phentolamine and yohimbine are both agents acting on alpha-adrenoceptors, again without a beta-blocking component to control tachycardia.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a combined alpha- and beta-adrenoceptor-blocking pair (phentolamine plus nadolol) as the appropriate pharmacotherapy for pheochromocytoma, over an alpha-only combination.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Phentolamine + nadolol"

questions.title: Alpha1 receptors raise IP3, DAG and calcium
questions.question: Stimulation of which of the following autonomic receptors would be expected to increased IP3 and DAG "second messengers" resulting in rise of calcium?

explanations.A: Correct. Alpha1-adrenoceptors are Gq-protein-coupled receptors. Their stimulation activates phospholipase C, generating the second messengers IP3 and DAG, and IP3 releases calcium from intracellular stores, raising cytosolic calcium. This IP3/DAG/calcium pathway is specific to Gq-coupled receptors like alpha1.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Beta2-adrenoceptors are Gs-coupled, signalling through adenylyl cyclase and cAMP, not the IP3/DAG/calcium pathway.
explanations.C: Incorrect. D1 dopamine receptors are also Gs-coupled, raising cAMP rather than IP3/DAG/calcium.
explanations.D: Incorrect. M2 acetylcholine receptors are Gi-coupled, decreasing cAMP, not signalling through IP3/DAG/calcium.

questions.learning_objective: Identify alpha1-adrenoceptor stimulation as the receptor pathway that raises IP3, DAG and intracellular calcium, among Gs- and Gi-coupled alternatives.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: A1 - adrenergic receptors."

questions.title: Phentolamine decreases BP by nonselective alpha blockade
questions.question: 14 years old Ms. Fahima was brought at casualty of Dammam Central Hospital, Surgical ward. At day-0, surgeon started IV injection of Phentolamine Mesylate for this patient. Phentolamine was used in this patient, because:

options.C: It decreases BP by blocking receptors, both alpha 1 and alpha 2
options.D: It increases BP by increasing peripheral resistance

explanations.A: Incorrect. Phentolamine is not an anxiolytic; it has no meaningful action on the receptor systems anxiolytics target.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Phentolamine is not an antipsychotic; its clinical use here is as an alpha-adrenoceptor antagonist, not a CNS dopamine-receptor-blocking agent.
explanations.C: Correct. Phentolamine is a nonselective alpha-adrenoceptor antagonist, blocking both alpha1 and alpha2 receptors. Blocking alpha1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle produces vasodilation, and this combined alpha1/alpha2 blockade is how phentolamine lowers blood pressure. This nonselective mechanism is why it is used for acute, reversible alpha blockade in a surgical or hypertensive-crisis setting.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This reverses phentolamine's actual effect -- it decreases, rather than increases, blood pressure and peripheral resistance, by blocking rather than stimulating alpha receptors.

questions.learning_objective: State that phentolamine lowers blood pressure through nonselective blockade of both alpha1 and alpha2 receptors.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It decreases BP by blocking receptors, both alpha 1" (option text truncates mid-sentence in the extracted PDF; completed as "both alpha 1 and alpha 2" per phentolamine's standard nonselective mechanism -- the other three options are unambiguously wrong regardless)

questions.title: Prazosin IS beneficial in BPH -- the false statement
questions.question: 28 years old Mr. Nagy was hypertensive since last 5 years. He came to GP at King Fahd Hospital for his treatment. GP prescribed tablet prazosin (5 mg) OD for him, for three days. Regarding PRAZOSIN, one is false:

options.A: It is not beneficial in patients with BPH
options.B: Dizziness and fainting occurs as "1st DOSE EFFECT"

explanations.A: Correct as the FALSE statement. Prazosin, an alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonist, IS beneficial in patients with BPH, since alpha1 blockade relaxes prostatic and bladder-neck smooth muscle. The statement that it is 'not beneficial' in BPH is therefore false -- prazosin is a recognised BPH treatment option, not a contraindicated one. This is the option the question asks to identify.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the answer (this statement is TRUE). Dizziness and fainting as a 'first-dose effect' is a well-recognised, true feature of prazosin therapy, from its abrupt initial vasodilation.
explanations.C: Incorrect as the answer (this statement is TRUE). Prazosin does dilate both arterioles and veins, lowering peripheral resistance and venous return.
explanations.D: Incorrect as the answer (this statement is TRUE). Prazosin does cause postural hypotension, most pronounced with the first dose, a known adverse effect of its vasodilating action.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that prazosin IS beneficial in BPH, recognising the false statement among prazosin's arteriolar/venous dilation, first-dose postural hypotension and BPH benefit.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It is not beneficial in patients with BPH" (marked as the FALSE statement)
